title.label: A beautiful way to manage your day

content.label: Love this app, it’s a gorgeous app that just makes sense to use. Incredibly well thought out and just so stable, I can always rely on Things 3 to catch me when my life gets busy!

title.label: Very disappointed very limited it at all useless

content.label: This app offers for less than Apple reminders. All you seem to be able to do is create tasks and sub tasks all of which you can do in Reminders plus a lot more for free. For instance you can add images in Reminders which you simply cannot do in this I feel it is a bit of a con because it really does not offer anything above and beyond the free app the Apple give you anyway so is pointless spending £10 for something that doesn’t quite do half of a free app bu pay for the privilege of using less functionality. You are even stuck with the first tier of headings that you can neither delete or change if unsuitably named. No benefits here just whatsoever stick with reminders and save yourself some money.

title.label: Great app, but no End-to-end Client-Side encryption

content.label: I’ve referred this app to lots of senior business colleagues, but later rescinded my recommendation because there’s no client-side end to end encryption.  Things is a great app, but confidentiality of contents is important for business users.

They really need a Windows app. My workflow involves both Mac and Windows and, while the app for iOS and Mac is great, I dislike having to use another device just to have task management. If they release a windows app, I’ll definitely come back.

title.label: wonderful app and a solid Getting Things Done experience

content.label: i tell you what this is a marvelous todo application, i’m loving it and the Shortcuts it provides i have one that lets me capture my location along with a note pinned as a widget to my home screen i love it

Nice looking and the one off pricing is attractive given nobody really has to pay for a decent to do  list app anymore (Reminders, Tasks, ToDo etc, all free). But with so many others out there and a lack of integrations or next level features it feels a bit of dead end. If you want a nice looking basic to do list and are happy to pay something for a certain refinement, it’s a good option, though Reminders is much improved. Not for those trying to creat a more sophisticated productivity stack.
Easy to use, visually great, find it helps my ADHD.

I really like the app, it has a modern feel and is really easy to use however one thing that’s quite annoying. I use the widget as a main part of my Home Screen, the large one, and each day it tells me I have nothing due as it doesn’t refresh until I open the Things app. Would be good if this refreshed for the morning without me having to open the app. Just a small bit of feedback, otherwise great work. Thanks
A must and a one off fee

I never write app reviews but I can’t overstate how happy I am with this product - even with the large (one-off) fee. I’m a GP in the UK and I have multiple work management, home management and learning goals to prioritise and execute (to be clear, this app is NOT suitable for any confidential information and my clinical work is entirely managed within our secure IT system at work). I’ve been looking for a product like this for a long time but was put off by the cost of Things 3 but I followed other reviewers advice and went online to the website and set up a two week free trial. The set-up process took about three hours to capture and organise all my commitments and I felt immensely relieved at the end of it. After a few days, I was convinced enough to buy the product outright. Two weeks later and my brain no longer has obligations rattling around in it and I’m getting through work at a great rate because tasks are already there to do. I tend to look through the ‘Anytime’ folder at the end of the day and schedule some tasks for the next day. I created several areas for different projects and also a ‘waiting for’ area. Highly recommend this product.
Purchased this app hoping my partner and I can have shared task lists together. But there is no such a feature. Just. A. Standard. Task. List.

title.label: Home Screen widget can’t self update

content.label:
Things has this odd cult following that claims it to be the best task app and cannot be surpassed. 

Here’s the thing, it’s pretty, it’s basic and the devs exploit this odd cult following through high prices and slow development. 

Big example is the home screen widget that won’t self update in the morning with todays tasks and when you open the app and close again, it might update, it might not. 

Contact the devs to report a bug and they claim it’s outside what they can do, which is odd because other task apps do this, so do weather apps and sport score apps. 

Lazy developers and a weird cult of users.
It’s a little too dull and I always want to press the bright red cancel button instead. Please make the DONE button bright blue or something. Thanks

title.label: So close to being really great

content.label: This is a lovely looking app, with very smooth operation and great UX, however the main disappointment is that you cannot add attachments or links and therefore it just becomes a good “checklist” app but can’t be used for ongoing or complicated tasks/to-do’s.

title.label: Changed the way I organise entirely

content.label: Really surprised by how this app and its desktop equivalent have changed my workflow for the better. So many nice little touches make this really easy to use

title.label: Pretty good, but the annoyances remain

content.label:
Annoyances still remain:

 If you accidentally tap or drag the “New Task” button (seems to happen to me a lot) and don’t enter any text, I would expect to be able to tap away and for the task to just not exist. Instead you have to manually delete it.

When you want to set a quick reminder, if you select a time that’s before the time on the current day, then it just ignores you. This is marginally better than when it used to yell at you. But if I want to quickly set a reminder for tomorrow, I need to go into the calendar, pull down, type something vaguely 9 like and then select 9am tomorrow. It’s the most work I’ve ever had to do to use a natural language input. Things should be letting me type once in the task description and detecting stuff like reminder times and deadlines. Please just release Things 4 with these fixes and I’ll happily pay for it.
In a world where every app is trying to do everything, Things is a breath of fresh air. A native app that really does help you get things done.

First time I’ve ever written a review for an app. But I felt compelled to write one after struggling with task management apps similar to this one. The design of the app is very clean and easy to use as an uncluttered clean look. Chris on support has been excellent with a few questions.. it’s very reasonably priced. User friendly and intuitive to use. It’s a pleasure to use. Mac version is excellent and phone.

This is like an old typewriter versus a modern word processor. A serious design flaw.
Not impressed at all. Simply isn’t what it should or could be.

Things app is fundamental to my life. Use it for 2 weeks and you’ll see why. I can remember everything I need to remember and what I need to do. I just wish … one wish … I could stick a photo in the notes. I’m always referencing things and a photographic reference is often essential. So I have to cross-reference to another app. But thank you for making life so darn simple.

I am still wondering and discovering little details everywhere during my usage of this app. Really kudos to the team, I have never seen such carefully designed app. However, I have some feedback: (1) As a first time user, I was confused how all sections worked at first, and still after one week. It might be useful to hide somethings for first time users and then suggest to show them after they get used to the app and according to their usage. (2) It is very useful to show calendar events with todos, but this is not available in widgets. PLEASE ADD IT! It’s super useful and allows me to have the same narrative outside and inside app. Please give me the last point to give you one additional star in return :)

Actually, despite the title, this app is brilliant. Full stop. It has amped up my productivity no end, and it is so easy and intuitive to use would thoroughly recommend this app to anyone who wants to download the clutter of their brain to a piece of software.
The only drawback, is I wish there was a shortcut to add a “To Do” from the control centre (like there is for Notes). This would make it that much faster to add a reminder that pops into your head on the go :) Great stuff, Things Team!

If you want a really simple task organiser, Things3 is great. Although expensive to use on several devices, it has a lovely clean interface, and syncs really well. It’s actually a pleasure to use. 

But … it’s a bit limited, especially if you like to plan ahead. 
When I look at my tasks due Tomorrow, they appear in a completely random order that can’t be changed. 
Apparently applying a basic sort order (e.g. by project!!) has been logged as a feature request. 
But there is no transparency about this — let alone a published development backlog or roadmap. 

After enjoying my experience with Things, I’ll be moving on soon to something a lot more flexible. I wish I’d chosen that route in the first place — it would have saved me a lot of time & money.

From the description it looks very promising.
Any instructions how to ise it?

title.label: Doesn’t work on Apple Watch Series 2

content.label: I’ve been using this for years and love it; however it stopped working on my Apple Watch Series 2 on the latest OS that support it (WatchOS 6), it simply don’t sync and gives me an error. I know it’s an “old” watch, but can’t help to feel a bit disappointed.
Revolutionary for me, it works, it’s easy, it’s user friendly, it links with email. Better than any other I have tried
Great app and wonderful design. Just wish there was a web app!

title.label: Settled on this for the UI alone

content.label: This does the same thing as every other GTD type task manager, but the thing that made me settle on it after trying countless others was it’s UI. It’s clean, clear and satisfying to use. It may be missing some more advanced features but I am willing to sacrifice that for the user experience. I’m sure many more features will come.
My brain finally has a place to put things!  I get to add ‘things’ via Siri and organise it later when the kids give me a moment to do it.  I feel like I can spin a lot more plates now.

title.label: Pretty good app. Expensive, but clean and easy.

content.label: Go for it if you have that sort of money and need an easy place to organize your life.

I really hate it when a perfectly good app like Things gets enhancements that break existing functionality. I’ve never had a problem with syncing Things tasks between my Mac, iPhone and Apple Watch. Now that syncing just doesn’t work consistently and previous Siri commands either no longer work or again do not sync properly across all my devices. Highly disappointing.

title.label: Lots of features, with a lot of thought in the interface

content.label: I like that the tutorial system makes use of its own task system, I feel like I’m achieving something as I try out each feature it instructs me on. I like the big plus button in the corner for quickly adding tasks and projects. So far a pretty neat experience.
I’m enjoying my time using it and despite straying to other apps find myself coming back. This is a simple, easy and quick to use app. The one thing I’d like to see is natural language input
Just the best designed task manager and there's no subscription to worry about

title.label: This is what apple watch needs

content.label:
Finally I found a solution for having reminders appears in apple watch complication. Also I was looking for an app which allows me to edit the reminders not just tick as done. 
Things3 is what you need! 👍

The level of detail in this app is amazing. 

Calendar feels better than my actual Callander.

The app is powerful, what it can do for people is life changing. 

Just please never close or stop. Please think of scenarios where business continuity problems stop this app from being available and working  in like 2037 and remove the issues. Money, deaths, disaster etc 

I want to be using this app forever.
Perfect for managing multiple businesses and projects in each. Syncs great between phone and iPad too

title.label: Fantastic little app - from desktop to phone

content.label:
This app is so intuitive and simple. Much better than some of the big expensive competitors that have endless levels of complexity - self-defeating when trying to improve productivity and efficiency! 
Things simply does the job - everything I need to keep myself organised both personally and professionally.
Works well. Fast sync. Easy to use.

Setting time within an app is easy - not in this app. 

Although I like the app, I cannot award more than three stars until the software engineers make setting time easy.
I have been a long time user of Todoist, then I entered the Apple world. Things is just simply the easiest GTD platform without having to adapt your app to conform. It just GTD.
I’ve tried them all (really!) and this is the best by far. Been using it since the first days of development. A real game changer. Seriously!

Been using a week and I think this a great little app - I needed a place where I could run a rolling to do list - this seems to do the job well - I know there are lots on market - but just something simple that sits on my Home Screen showing number of tasks to do is all I needed

title.label: So glad to be back to Things!

content.label: Had used Things in its early days… a decade ago, and had migrated to other systems. So glad to be back to Things - really intuitive, interacts with other apps really well… and helps keep me on track with multiple projects and tasks. Simply Brilliant app!

title.label: Brilliant but crying out for new features.

content.label:
I really do love Things 3, I have it for Mac and iPhone and use everyday. It has been too long since there’s been any significant feature upgrades now, would be great if you shared your roadmap. 

The ability to upload images/files would be super helpful. 

The ability to forward iMessages into the app in the same way as spark emails can be. 

Location based reminders would be a helpful.

A calendar view with time blocking feature would be helpful. (I like that ical inputs pull through) but would be good to see Things inputs alongside iCal inputs on a Things calendar view. 

Moving the move, tag and time/date buttons to the top would save having to scroll to the bottom of a long entry that has been forwarded from email. This is a frustrating UX experience. 

Please give us a clue on what’s being worked on, I’m sure it would result in more sales.

title.label: It’s actually really good but no Windows support? 😤

content.label:
This would be a 5 star reciew but as I’m one of a few people who use an iPhone yet has a windows laptop for compatibility with most of the platforms used for my work.

I love this app and have very little complaints but the most painful thing is there is I can’t use it on my laptop. 😒 Please expand, with the money you charge you surely are able to!

title.label: Perfect tool for getting stuff done

content.label:
Easy to use once you get the hang of it, practically the best productivity tool I have ever used designed to make your life easier

Please add a calendar to help schedule time blocks
Looks good but not as powerful as some other To Do apps. Also expensive especially if you want to use across devices.

title.label: Super easy to learn. Organisation made simple!

content.label: Excellent app. Tried many others. Things makes to do lists and project planning a doddle. It could not be easier, faster or more intuitive. Try it. You’ll love it.

I love this app and have been using it for a couple of years, religiously every day. 

It’s easy to use, quick to use, and a joy to use. It enables me to organise my life and work, and ensure I don’t forget anything I need to do, nor spend all day organising it. 

My only suggestions are two-fold:
1) swipe down from Today to lead into Upcoming, so I can see what’s next
2) I’m not going to lie, it’s expensive. I have it for iPhone and iPad (and you have to pay twice) but I haven’t quite stomached the money to get the Mac version yet. That said, you only pay once, no subscription required, so it works out as good value in the long run. 

I probably will eventually purchase the Mac app for my new MacBook Pro as it is that good!
